Compiler Design

This page describes each phase of the Nabu compiler in detail, from parsing source files to emitting bytecode. ## Pipeline overview
The core driver is the `NabuCompiler` class (in `compiler`), which implements `tools.Compiler`. Its `compile(CompilerOptions)` method drives the frontend (`processFiles`), and `generateCode` drives the backend. ## Frontend phases ### Parse Source files are dispatched by file-extension *kind* to a registered `SourceParser` / `LanguageParser` via the plugin registry. The compiler supports parsing multiple languages (Nabu, Java, Kotlin) and mixing them in one project. Each parser produces an abstract syntax tree (`CompilationUnit`). The Nabu language uses ANTLR grammars (`NabuLexer.g4` / `NabuParser.g4`) plus the `NabuCompilerVisitor` (~3,300 lines) which builds the AST. ### Enter The `EnterPhase` / `EnterClasses` adds classes to the symbol table. This happens before resolution so that classes can be resolved when referenced by other classes (independent of source order). ### Resolve The `ResolverPhase` resolves classes, methods, fields, and other symbols. It reads class files via ASM (`resolve/asm`), handles generics, method resolution (`resolve/method`), boxing, and type entering. This is a broad phase that gives the compiler a full symbol and type model. ### Annotate The `AnnotatePhase` de-proxies annotations and provides annotation-processing interoperability. It runs JSR-269-style processors through a `JavacProcessingEnvironment` with a `JavacFiler`, `JavacElements`, `JavacTypes`, `JavacMessager`, and `JavacRoundEnvironment`. See [Annotation Processing](/annotation-processing/) for details. ### Transform The `TransformPhase` runs `CodeTransformer`s registered as compiler plugins. This is where DSLs hook in — for example, the JPA plugin transforms a readable criteria DSL into standard JPA calls. See [DSL Support](/plugins/dsl-support/). ### Check The `CheckPhase` performs type and flow diagnostics and checks for unresolved symbols (methods, fields, types). ### LambdaToMethod The `LambdaToMethodPhase` desugars lambda expressions into synthetic private methods via SAM conversion (using `invokedynamic` / `LambdaMetafactory`-style lowering). ## Backend phases ### Lower The `Lower` phase adds additional code: - Generate code to init fields (both in constructors and in ``) - Generate code for enum and record classes (`EnumCodeGenerator`, `RecordCodeGenerator`) - Add boxing and unboxing code - Lower enhanced-for statements - Remap enum switches ### IR generation The `IrGeneratingVisitor` builds an intermediate representation from the lowered AST. The `ir` package contains: - **`IRModule`** — flags, name, super type, interfaces, sealed classes, fields, functions, globals - **`IRFunction`** — name, return type, parameters, basic blocks - **`IRBasicBlock`** — label, instructions, successors, termination - **`IRInstruction`** — Alloca, AllocaArray, ArrayLoad/Store, BinaryOp, Branch, Call, Cast, CondBranch, HeapAlloc, IndirectCall, InstanceOf, Load, MonitorEnter/Exit, Move, Phi, Pop, Return, Store, Throw, TryCatchRegion - **`IRValue`** — ConstBool, ConstClass, ConstFloat, ConstInt, ConstNull, ConstString, FunctionRef, Named, Temp - **`IRType`** — Array, Bool, Float, Function, Int, Ptr, Struct, Void ### IR optimization The IR is optimized through several passes in `backend/ir`: - **`SsaBuilder`** — Cytron-style SSA construction (dominance tree, dominance frontiers, phi placement, renaming) - **`PhiElimination`** — replaces phis with stores in predecessors and loads in the head block - **`Linearizer`** — orders blocks and inverts conditions for fall-through - **`Optimizer`** — runs an optimization pipeline: TypeInference → ConstantFolder → CopyPropagation → GVN → DCE, repeated to a fixpoint (max 10 iterations) The IR is **backend-agnostic** — all backends consume the same `IRModule`, which is the key to the "write a language once, target multiple backends" design. ### Bytecode emission The IR module is handed to a registered `Backend` which emits class files. See the [Backends](/backends/) section for the details of each backend. - Class files are emitted at **version 61 (Java 17)** by default (`JavaVersion.MINIMAL_VERSION`), up to `V23`. - The default **ASM backend** is slot-based (JVM local-variable-slot addressed) and validated via `CheckClassAdapter`. ## Module layout | Module | Responsibility | |---|---| | `compiler-api` | Public API/SPI layer (AST, type system, tools, language SPI, element model, resolve SPI, transform SPI) | | `compiler` | Core compiler: parse, enter, resolve, transform, check, lower, IR, ASM backend | | `nabu-lang` | Nabu language: ANTLR grammar + `NabuCompilerVisitor` | | `java-backend` | Experimental backend using the JDK 24 ClassFile API | | `native-backend` | Experimental LLVM-based native backend | | `maven-plugin` | Maven plugin wiring the compiler into builds | | `jpa-plugin` / `jpa-support` | Example DSL plugin for JPA criteria | | `nabu-daemon` / `nabu-client` | Compile daemon protocol for incremental builds | | `tools` | Project-model tooling | | `testing` | Scaffold for testing compiler plugins |
